attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Is going to become untenable' is firm language, so this is a scored forecast with no deadline. The normalisation drops 'for those raising it' but keeps the core prediction and the stated cause (11%+ rates, meagre margins).

contract.note: The plain reading (widespread failure to service or refinance, not one failed project) is ordinary and fair. Requiring actual borrowing costs, not just secondary-market yields, matches the stated mechanism. The early-resolution rule is reasonable.

evidence.note: Reuters, Oct 2026: a CoreWeave bond's yield briefly passed 16% and default-insurance costs spiked. This is market stress, not proof of defaults, refinancing at 11%+, or failure across the sector.
CoreWeave's own Aug 2026 announcement of an oversubscribed loan priced at SOFR+5.5%. Temporary access to credit cannot refute an open-ended 'eventually' forecast.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet shows market stress, but no representative set of defaults, distressed restructurings or failed financings that is tied to 11%+ borrowing costs and thin margins. The early-resolution rule is not met, and a successful financing does not refute 'eventually'. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate in his own post.

semantics.note: This is a conditional estimate that keeps the faster-than-OpenAI assumption. The drafter's modality field says 'likely', but the speaker used no hedge. The proposition itself is faithful.

contract.note: Measuring realised calendar-2026 revenue and a ±10% band for 'around' is an ordinary reading. How 'growing faster' is defined (period, percentage) was supplied by the evaluator, not the speaker, and could decide the result.

evidence.note: CNBC, citing Bloomberg: Q1 $4.73B and Q2 ~$11.5B, which matches the ~$16.3B first-half premise. It gives no full-year result and no comparison with OpenAI's growth.

reviews.rationale: The forecast covers full-year 2026, which had not ended by 2026-10-28. Whether the antecedent (faster growth than OpenAI) held is unknown. No readable evidence shows cumulative realised revenue above $44B, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Not scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, presenting the output of his own model.

semantics.note: This is a model-based estimate of cost and margins. The 'per my model' framing and the full-occupancy, no-debt assumptions are kept. The literal '$12.10 a megawatt' is preserved; it is probably a typo for $12.10 million.

contract.note: Requiring the model to be reproduced, plus comparable independent inputs, is fair. Unclear units, revenue period, and IT load versus total facility power leave the result dependent on interpretation.

evidence.note: JLL: shell construction about $11.3M/MW in 2026, with tech fit-out up to $25M/MW. Its cost coverage and capacity definition are not matched to the model, and it does not test the margins.

reviews.rationale: The model was paywalled or only partly accessible, so its arithmetic cannot be reproduced. The only independent benchmark does not match the model's equipment, capacity basis or margin definition. The speaker's assertion cannot prove itself. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The testable core is a present exposure estimate: AI startups make up ~60–80% of the two labs' enterprise revenue. 'Even less likely to be able to pay' is probabilistic wording and cannot be scored. Framing it as a conditional forecast that waits for the startups to disappear makes it effectively untestable.

contract.note: The contract sets aside a current customer-revenue breakdown as non-resolving, even though that breakdown is the ordinary way to test the claim. It also requires the startups to actually depart. That stretches the claim away from its plain present-tense meaning.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 (Oct 26, 2026) says its customers include AI-native startups. It gives no revenue share for startups.

Ramp sample: 80% of observed spending comes from 1% of firms. This is a different population and denominator; those firms are not identified as startups, and it is not the labs' total enterprise revenue.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not show what share of either lab's enterprise revenue comes from startups, so the 60–80% exposure cannot be tested. Under the drafter's conditional framing, the antecedent has not occurred. The 'less likely to pay' part is hedged and cannot be scored. Unresolved either way.
